title: MakeMyTrip Acquires Majority Stake In Quick Ride To Enter Ride Pooling
summary: MakeMyTrip acquires majority stake in Quick Ride to enter the carpooling market
detailed: MakeMyTrip acquired a majority stake in Bengaluru-based ride-pooling startup Quick Ride for an undisclosed amount.
Quick Ride's brand and business were transferred to a new entity, Co Ride Mobility Private Limited, while its EV taxi business remains with its predecessor.
Quick Ride serves enterprise clients and operates in eight Indian cities, having raised over $14 million previously from investors.
This acquisition matters by expanding MakeMyTrip's ground transportation portfolio into high-frequency daily intra-city commutes and intercity travel.
sentences: Quick Ride’s promoters will continue to lead the business.
However, Quick Ride’s erstwhile electric vehicle (EV) taxi business will remain with its predecessor entity, iDisha Info Labs Pvt Ltd.
Founded in 2014 by KNM Rao, Quick Ride offers a ride-sharing application that connects passengers to riders.
It connects the commuters travelling in the same direction.
It also offers an enterprise solution for shared mobility and counts IT companies such as Wipro, TCS, Infosys, IBM and Cognizant, among others as its clients.
Its services are available in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune, Kochi, Delhi NCR, Mumbai, and Kolkata.
The startup has raised over $14 Mn from investors like Sequoia, Prosus and Venture Highway.
The Quick Ride acquisition is part of MakeMyTrip’s broader strategy to expand its presence across adjacent travel and mobility segments through strategic investments and acquisitions.

Commenting on the acquisition, MakeMyTrip group CEO Rajesh Magow said that the investment would help the company establish a presence in daily intra-city commutes while strengthening its intercity travel offerings.

“As part of our expansion strategy, we have pursued selective strategic partnerships, investments and acquisitions that complement and strengthen our existing business and expand the breadth and depth of our offerings.
Ride pooling gives us a presence in high-frequency daily commutes within cities, as well as intercity travel,” he added.
The company plans to leverage its experience in building redBus across India and overseas markets to scale Quick Ride’s ride-pooling business.

In the past few years, MakeMyTrip has acquired Savaari to strengthen its car rental services, Happay in corporate travel and expense management, and Flamingo Transworld in regional group holiday packages.
It has also made a strategic minority investment in visa processing platform Atlys.

The development comes as MakeMyTrip looks to deepen its presence across the travel value chain, moving beyond conventional travel bookings towards a broader set of transportation and ancillary services.
On the financial front, the travel tech major’s consolidated net profit for the three months ended June 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27) plunged 65% to $9.1 Mn from $25.8 Mn in the year-ago period.
MakeMyTrip’s revenue grew 6% YoY to $285.6 Mn.
